02 / WHY THIS ROLE FITS

The responsibilities.
The experience behind them.

An AI application succeeds when the technology, the people and the operating processes work together. That is the intersection I work in.

OWN THE APPLICATION. SUPPORT THE USER.

Practical fluency in core legal AI.

The role calls for

Owning core legal AI applications, supporting enterprise AI tools, triaging attorney questions, troubleshooting and escalating issues appropriately.

I bring

Hands-on agent building in Harvey, Legora and Wordsmith AI, alongside legal technology consulting and experience developing guidance for attorney workflows.

How I would put it to work

Clarify the legal task, reproduce the issue with appropriate test data, resolve what I can, and give the vendor or internal team a clear escalation with an owner and follow-up.

TEST WITH A PURPOSE. RELEASE WITH CARE.

Experience moving from idea to implementation.

The role calls for

Coordinating feature tests, integrations and workflow rollouts; keeping up with product releases, feature launches and licensing changes.

I bring

GenAI implementation coordination and quality assurance across four MHC offices, legal output evaluation frameworks, and rapid prototyping through agent projects and hackathons.

How I would put it to work

Define success criteria, test representative matters, document limitations and permissions, and turn release or licensing changes into concise guidance for attorneys and leadership.

MAKE THE VALUE VISIBLE.

Communication that helps people change how they work.

The role calls for

Tracking usage, adoption, feedback and business value; delivering communications, demos and training that improve responsible adoption and return on investment.

I bring

Attorney guidance and knowledge repositories at MHC, law-firm AI governance presentations at INTLDA, and a firm-wide AI knowledge seminar at DLA Piper. I received Eversheds Sutherland’s Best Speaker Award in 2025.

How I would put it to work

Pair usage data with lawyer feedback and task-level measures: output quality, review effort, completion time and repeat use. Use the findings to improve training and prioritise useful workflows.

CLEAR GUIDANCE. CLEAR OWNERSHIP.

Governance that connects to daily decisions.

The role calls for

Maintaining governance, policies, documentation and support processes; partnering with IT, KM, Innovation, Security, Risk and business teams; coordinating vendor issues and follow-up.

I bring

AI governance advisory work with law firms at INTLDA, presentations on ABA Formal Opinion 512, human-in-the-loop governance work at Fledger and cross-office stakeholder coordination at MHC.

How I would put it to work

Maintain a clear record of approved uses, review expectations, issues and decisions. Connect attorney needs to the right technical, risk and vendor owners, and keep open items moving.

UNDERSTAND THE WHOLE WORKFLOW.

Curiosity grounded in legal practice.

The role calls for

Evaluating integrations with document systems, knowledge tools, Microsoft 365 and other firm platforms, while identifying emerging AI capabilities relevant to legal work.

I bring

Legal technology evaluation covering AI, electronic discovery and information governance, agent-building experience, Microsoft Office proficiency and a general understanding of IT systems, networking and software.

How I would put it to work

Map the information flow, permissions, source quality and human review points before recommending an integration. Test new capabilities against a concrete attorney need and the firm’s operating requirements.

07 / LOOKING AHEAD

How I would get started.

A proposed first 90 days, shaped around the firm’s priorities, existing systems and feedback from its lawyers.

DAYS 01–30

Listen & map

Understand the tools, licences, support routes and governance. Meet key stakeholders, observe attorney workflows and establish an adoption baseline.

DAYS 31–60

Test & enable

Prioritise useful workflows, coordinate focused pilots, document recurring support issues and deliver concise, practice-specific demonstrations.

DAYS 61–90

Measure & improve

Review usage and feedback, assess quality and review effort, refine training and recommend the next set of improvements with clear owners.
